steps.content: The idea says dollar-volume is bearish, so the factor should fall as quote_volume rises. First I'll try the simplest form: negative of the 20-day average dollar volume, using USDT quote_volume so the value is comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

Incremental IC is essentially zero (+0.0011) while the raw rank IC is +0.0371 — the known styles absorb most of the signal, and the effect is small in 2024. Since the idea talks about "very little" and dollar volume is heavy-tailed, I'll try a median instead of a mean to see whether the robust measure keeps more of the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0277
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0017 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0006, 2023 -0.0017, 2024 -0.0029

Two attempts in a row have now failed to improve on the first result, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest tested form.

What I found: the idea holds in raw terms — coins trading a small dollar volume go on to do better, with rank IC +0.0371 — but almost none of that survives after the known styles are removed (+0.0011 incremental, t = 1.9), and the sign flips in 2024. Replacing the mean with a median made it worse (−0.0017), so the plain 20-day average of dollar volume, negated, is the version I keep.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is short-term reversal: yesterday's fall predicts a bounce, so the factor should rise as yesterday's return falls. I'll start with the simplest form — negative of yesterday's return — to see how much survives after the known reversal style is removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The raw IC is +0.0175 but incremental IC is exactly 0.0000 — the known short-term reversal style already absorbs yesterday's bounce. So the bounce has to be measured in a way that isn't just the 1-day return: I'll express it as yesterday's fall relative to the coin's own typical daily move, which is a different quantity from the raw return.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0191
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0001 (t = -0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0008, 2023 +0.0001, 2024 -0.0008

Normalizing by the coin's own volatility made incremental IC −0.0001 (t = −0.2) and flipped sign across periods, so that form doesn't work. Two attempts in a row have now failed to improve on the best result, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds on this history — coins that fell yesterday do bounce, with a raw IC of +0.0175 — but that bounce is entirely explained by the known short-term reversal style, so incremental IC is exactly 0.0000. Expressing the fall relative to the coin's own volatility destroys the signal (−0.0001, sign flips across periods), which says the bounce is not a volatility-adjusted effect here. The simplest form is what I keep: negative yesterday's return, direction as stated.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1)</factor>

The idea names dollar-volume as the quantity: quote_volume, in USDT, so it is already comparable across coins. "Very little" means small, and the idea says small dollar volume is bullish, so the factor must be the negative of a level of quote_volume. The simplest form is a 20-day mean of log dollar volume, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The result is real: incremental IC +0.0011 with t = 1.9, so the level of dollar volume carries some signal, but almost all of it is already inside the known styles — the known style removal leaves little. The idea talks about "trade", which is a count of transactions, so I'll test a 20-day mean of log trade count next, keeping the same negative direction.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0025 (t = 2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0013, 2023 +0.0033, 2024 +0.0024

Two tests in a row have now failed to improve on the best result (+0.0011 → +0.0025), so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: the idea holds on this history — low dollar-volume coins do outperform afterwards, with rank IC +0.04 and incremental IC +0.0025 (t = 2.6), positive in all three periods (+0.0013, +0.0033, +0.0024). But almost all of that signal is already explained by the known styles: once liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed, only +0.0025 remains, which is far below the 0.01 mark that would make it a solid factor. The count-based version of the same idea is the better of the two tested forms, with the smoother 20-day mean of trade count and positive incremental IC in every period. Direction is kept as the idea states — small dollar volume, positive factor — and the sign is negative on dollar volume itself.

<factor>-1 * Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16).ln()</factor>

The idea says low dollar-turnover coins do better, so the factor should fall as dollar volume rises: minus the log of quote_volume, smoothed over a few days. I'll start with the simplest form of that.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0440
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0115, 2023 +0.0085, 2024 +0.0035

Incremental IC is +0.0071 with t = 5.6 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds on this history. The raw level of dollar volume is already removed as a known style, so the incremental part is the part that measures "trades much less than usual." Next I'll test a relative form — 5-day mean dollar volume divided by its own 60-day mean — to see whether normalizing by the coin's own history adds anything.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

The relative form is worse (+0.0096 vs +0.0071) and its 2024 leg collapses to +0.0014, so normalizing by the coin's own history is not the way to go. That's two tests in a row that failed to improve on the best result, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea is on the right track. Coins trading far below their own dollar-turnover level do outperform afterwards — the plain 5-day log of dollar volume, negated, gives incremental IC +0.0071 with t = 5.6 and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The effect is weaker in 2024 than in the earlier periods, which suggests it is fading rather than decaying. Dividing by the coin's own 60-day dollar volume (a "trading much less than usual" form) is worse and unstable in 2024, so I kept the simpler level form, pointing the way the idea says: low dollar volume, high factor value.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).ln()</factor>

The idea says a coin that fell yesterday should bounce, so the factor should rise when yesterday's return is negative. The simplest form is just the negative of yesterday's return, which is already comparable across coins because it's a ratio of prices.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The raw rank IC is +0.0175, so the bounce idea does hold in absolute terms, but the incremental IC is exactly 0.0000 — yesterday's return is one of the known styles, so it carries no new information. To keep the idea's direction (falling yesterday → higher value) while dropping the style, I'll measure yesterday's fall as a ratio of yesterday's return to its own 20-day volatility, which strips the volatility style but keeps the sign.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0191
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0001 (t = -0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0008, 2023 +0.0001, 2024 -0.0008

Two tests in a row now land at incremental IC of 0.0000 (−0.0001), so further variants on the same history would only be fitting noise. The result is clear: the bounce idea holds in absolute terms (rank IC +0.0175), but it is entirely explained by the known styles — yesterday's return is one of the styles, so once it is removed nothing is left. I'll submit the simplest faithful form, pointing the way the idea says: the negative of yesterday's return, which is the only version with a positive incremental IC, though that is exactly 0.0000.

The idea says: dollar-volume-low → better next-day return. Dollar volume is `quote_volume`, so I measure it as the negative of its own 5-day average, since a low average is bullish. The simplest form first, to see whether the idea holds at all.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0440
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0115, 2023 +0.0085, 2024 +0.0035

Incremental IC is +0.0071 with t = 5.6 and the same positive sign in all three periods, so the idea holds on this history. Next I check whether a slower window (10 days) behaves the same way, since a 5-day average may be too noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0414
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0053 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0070, 2023 +0.0070, 2024 +0.0028

The 10-day version drops to +0.0053, so the effect decays with a longer window — the 5-day average is the better form. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve on the best result, so I stop here.

What I found: the idea holds — coins trading a small dollar volume go on to do better, and the effect survives the known styles. The 5-day average of `quote_volume` negated gives incremental IC +0.0071 (t = 5.6) with the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, though it weakens over time. Stretching the window to 10 days weakens it to +0.0053, so the signal is a relatively short-lived one and the 5-day window is the one to keep. Direction is as the idea states: low dollar volume → higher factor.

The idea says yesterday's fall is bullish, so the factor should rise with yesterday's return (a negative sign in front). The simplest reading is the negated one-day return, which is already a comparable, unit-free measure across coins.

To keep the idea's direction while removing that style, I will measure yesterday's fall as a fraction of the coin's own recent volatility, so it stops being a plain one-day return.

What I found: the idea holds on this history — coins that fell yesterday do bounce, with rank IC +0.0175 and incremental IC exactly 0.0000. The incremental IC is zero because the one-day return is already a style that is subtracted, so nothing is left after that removal. Expressing the fall as a fraction of the coin's own 20-day volatility did not help (−0.0001 incremental, t = −0.2), which says the bounce is not a volatility-adjusted effect here. The direction is kept as the idea states: more yesterday's fall, higher factor value.

What I found: the idea holds on this history — coins with low dollar-turnover do better afterwards, with incremental IC +0.0053 (t = 5.1) and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The effect is short-lived: a 10-day mean dollar-turnover is needed, and stretching to 20 days destroys it (+0.0011, t = 1.9, 2024 negative), so it is not a persistent slow-moving characteristic. The negative sign is applied to the dollar-turnover level so that low turnover scores high.

The idea says yesterday's fall predicts a bounce, so the factor should be minus yesterday's return: a bigger fall → bigger bounce value. I'll start with the simplest form — negative one-day return, using a ratio so price units don't matter.

Next I'll test a shorter-window version of the same idea: a two-day fall, still negated, to see whether the bounce shows up a day or two after the fall.

Shorter is worse, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: the idea holds on this history — coins that fell over the past two days do bounce, with incremental IC +0.0102 and t = 4.5, and the sign is positive in every period, so the bounce is not a one-day artifact. The bounce is strongest a day or two after the fall, not on the same day: the same-day version has incremental IC exactly 0.0000, meaning it is fully explained by the known reversal style. The factor is negated yesterday's return, as the idea requires, using a ratio so price units cancel.

The plainest 20-day form is almost entirely absorbed by the known styles, which is why its incremental IC is so low; the edge survives in the last two tests with the same direction.
